choices.feedback: This uses “this.freqKeys.get(newFreq).set(null, null);” instead of “this.freqKeys.get(newFreq).set(key, null);”. On this test, it returns [null,null,null,1,null,-1,3,null,1,3,4]; the expected result is [null,null,null,1,null,-1,3,null,-1,3,4].

choices.label: Choose this statement
choices.feedback: This uses “this.freqKeys.get(newFreq).set(null, key);” instead of “this.freqKeys.get(newFreq).set(key, null);”. On this test, it returns [null,null,null,1,null,-1,3,null,1,3,4]; the expected result is [null,null,null,1,null,-1,3,null,-1,3,4].

choices.label: Choose this statement
choices.feedback: Store null under key “key” in the value stored for “newFreq” in “this.freqKeys”.

contextOnly.reason: The first insertion sets minFreq to 1 before a frequency bucket can be read. Missing-key get returns immediately, and zero-capacity put returns without using minFreq. This redundant initial value is shown in the constructor block.
